name: AECi — Home stats compute failed (daily cron)
message:
A `home.*` stats compute failed in the last day (AECI-178, daily 07:00 UTC = 02:00 EST cron). This fires when either the per-key `aeci.stats.compute.key{outcome:failed}` count OR the job-level `aeci.stats.compute{outcome:failed}` count is non-zero. The job-level term is load-bearing: a **pre-compute crash** (e.g. Prisma init / DB down) takes the inline catch in scheduled.ts and emits the job-level `outcome:failed` heartbeat but NO per-key points — and that same heartbeat keeps the companion 'not running' monitor green — so without this term a total crash would slip past both monitors. Each key computes/validates/upserts independently, so a single failed key leaves that one cached value stale (or absent) while the rest refresh — e.g. a failed `home.trending_products` keeps yesterday's list. Pivot the 'AECi Phase 4 — Home / Stats' dashboard by `key` to see which failed (a pre-compute crash names none), and read the `stats-cron` logs (`aeci.stats.compute <key> status=failed` with `reason`, or `aeci.stats.compute.crashed` for a pre-compute throw) for the cause.

Note: this monitor deliberately does NOT use notify_no_data — `outcome:failed` is absent on a healthy run, so no-data here would be a constant false alarm. Cron liveness ('did the daily compute run at all?') is the companion monitor 'AECi — Home stats not running', which watches the always-emitted `aeci.stats.compute{trigger:cron}` heartbeat via notify_no_data.

Runbook: https://github.com/the-wbs-project/aec-integrations/blob/main/docs/RUNBOOKS.md#home-stats-stale-or-compute-failed
